summary:
The dominant story across markets remains the US inflation-stagflation nexus driven by the Iran war. Core PCE printed at 3.3% year-over-year in April, in line with expectations, while the all-items PCE gauge hit 3.8% — a three-year high — with energy and tariffs the principal drivers alongside AI-related spending. First-quarter GDP was revised lower to 1.6%, a combination that has Chicago Fed President Goolsbee explicitly flagging a stagflationary trajectory. Gold has broken above $4,400 an ounce on rate-hike fears before pulling back slightly, and TIPS ETF inflows are surging even as analysts warn the instruments do not always track realized CPI cleanly.

Fed officials are navigating visibly divergent signals. Vice Chair Jefferson acknowledges upside inflation risks but expects tariff and energy effects to fade. New York Fed President Williams calls policy "well-positioned." Minneapolis Fed President Kashkari is more hawkish, warning that entrenched inflation expectations could force tougher action later. A reported US-Iran ceasefire extension briefly lifted Treasuries and weighed on the dollar against major peers, with Citadel Securities arguing markets are underpricing a Strait of Hormuz reopening relief rally. ECB President Lagarde meanwhile reiterated that Fed independence remains under threat.

In structured finance, CLO managers are pulling issuance forward to capture strong investor demand, per Octus pipeline data, while SEI is expanding its high-yield bond and CLO ETF lineup to meet retail appetite. The broader asset-backed finance market is being surveyed ahead of Global ABS 2026. A separate credit concern has emerged in leveraged loans: Avis's abrupt split with a SaaS vendor has crystallized fears about software-contract risk embedded in loan collateral, with Wall Street increasingly scrutinizing technology vendor concentration in deal underwriting.

On the sovereign and bank capital side, European lenders are issuing AT1 bonds at a record pace with unusually long call dates — locking in favorable funding costs for up to a decade. Argentine provinces are accessing global bond markets at the fastest rate in nearly a decade even as the federal government avoids external issuance ahead of the 2027 elections, and BCI is building out a dedicated private equity fund financing team to serve buyout firms starved of deal exit liquidity.

The dominant development this week is the ECB's pointed warning that financial markets are materially underpricing geopolitical and fiscal risks, with Vice President Luis de Guindos specifically cautioning that Washington's volatile trade posture and a potential U.S.-Iran military conflict could trigger a broader financial crisis. The warning lands as eurozone sovereign borrowers are already diversifying issuance away from euros, tapping dollar, Swiss franc, and other currency markets to broaden their investor base — a structural signal that European credit managers are hedging against domestic fragility.

On the macro front, U.S. bank fundamentals held firm in Q1 according to the FDIC, with key metrics improving despite elevated rates and geopolitical noise, though unrealized losses on securities portfolios edged higher. Canada's National Bank beat fiscal Q2 estimates on broad segment strength with lower-than-expected loan loss provisions, though shares sold off on valuation. UK consumers face renewed pressure as inflation is now projected to reach 3.6% in Q4, driven by rising energy costs.

In structured finance, Qdoba completed a $435 million whole business securitization, the latest in a series of franchise-backed ABS deals that package royalty streams and IP into rated tranches. The transaction underscores continued investor appetite for non-traditional collateral in the WBS format. Separately, Warner Bros. Discovery secured bondholder consent to amend existing debt covenants, clearing a critical path toward its $110 billion merger with Paramount Skydance. Skydance's Ellison family has privately committed to capping the combined entity's leverage, a verbal assurance aimed at keeping credit analysts onside ahead of formal closing.

In fintech, Zero Hash founder Edward Woodford confirmed the firm is pursuing a national trust bank charter, positioning the crypto infrastructure provider ahead of potential regulatory clarity under the CLARITY Act, which could significantly reshape licensing requirements for digital asset firms operating in the U.S.

The dominant theme across markets is the entrenchment of a higher real rate regime. Citadel Securities has openly called on the Federal Reserve to pivot back toward hiking, framing rising consumer prices — not growth slowdown — as the primary threat. The ECB echoed the risk-off warning from a different angle, cautioning that financial markets are materially underpricing geopolitical and fiscal risks, with Vice President de Guindos specifically flagging Washington's volatile trade posture and a potential Iran conflict as triggers for financial instability. UK inflation is now projected to hit 3.6% in Q4, squeezing household budgets via energy costs. The bond selloff, per current analysis, is being driven by elevated real rates rather than breakeven inflation alone — a structurally more durable headwind for duration.

In credit, eurozone sovereign borrowers are diversifying issuance into dollars and Swiss francs to access new investor pools, a tactical response to spread dynamics and rate differentials. Warner Bros. Discovery secured bondholder consent to amend debt terms ahead of its $110 billion merger with Paramount Skydance, while Ellison has privately committed to containing leverage at the combined entity — a signal the deal's credit profile is being actively managed before close.

Structured finance activity remains robust. Qdoba priced a $435 million whole business securitization to fund operational momentum, the latest in a string of restaurant-sector WBS deals. Mountain Point priced a $500 million algorithm-driven CLO, and Chenavari completed a refinancing of a tranche within its 2024 CLO capital stack, reflecting continued liability management appetite. Separately, securitization standards for mortgages and home equity products are under active review, and multilateral development banks are accelerating securitization programs to mobilize private capital.

On the macro-banking side, the FDIC reported improved key metrics at US lenders in Q1 despite a modest uptick in unrealized losses. In fintech, Zero Hash is pursuing a national trust bank charter as the CLARITY Act reshapes the US crypto regulatory landscape.

The dominant development across markets is the entrenchment of a higher-for-longer rate regime globally, amplified by the Iran conflict. Kevin Warsh has been sworn in as Federal Reserve Chair, and markets are pricing the opposite of what Trump originally intended — the Treasury curve's key yield gap has tightened to its tightest level in a year as traders bet on prolonged restraint. Fed minutes revealed internal support for rate hikes if inflation proves persistent, Fed Governor Waller said inflation risks mean the Fed should no longer signal cuts, and Bill Dudley called the case for cutting rates "very, very weak." Citadel Securities went further, arguing the Fed should pivot toward active tightening. BlackRock's Saigal sees "sufficient factors" for a cut, but Franklin Templeton's Desai countered that the market is not realistically pricing long-end yields. U.S. consumer sentiment hit a fresh record low in May, with the Hormuz blockade pushing fuel prices roughly 50% higher and squeezing household spending power. Treasury Secretary Bessent is described as having limited options to arrest the yield climb, with government borrowing costs at their highest since 2007. China, meanwhile, cut its one-year policy loan rate to a record low to counter slowing momentum.

In Europe, the ECB is firmly on a June hike trajectory. Executive Board member Isabel Schnabel said the ECB should raise rates next month regardless of any quick Middle East resolution. Chief Economist Philip Lane told Nikkei the ECB will likely raise its June inflation projections as elevated energy costs feed through. The Bank of France governor and Governing Council member Sleijpen echoed the commitment to doing "everything necessary." The ECB separately warned that a private-credit-fueled AI boom poses systemic risk, with a simulated severe shock showing European insurers and pension funds more exposed than banks. Korea flagged $37 billion in overseas private credit exposure for monitoring, and private credit default rates have hit a record high.

In structured finance, activity remains robust despite the macro headwind. FTAI Aviation priced its inaugural ABS securitization. Chenavari refinanced a slice of a 2024 CLO capital stack. U.S. BB CLO BWICs saw strong demand for higher-MVOC top-tier names. Securitization momentum is also building across multilateral development banks. The structured finance industry is simultaneously pushing for broader benchmark indices, and Channel completed its eighth ABS transaction.
